[A10] IMPLEMENTATION ASSIGNMENT

A173 Opus takes the sole author slot after A160 on #504 finishes. Independent cleared-context reviewers are R245 internal Opus and R246 external Codex. Starting dev is `483a133ed08867ea0d300d2b4a027b5b48a4282f`. The public issue body freezes the two-worker ordinary-simulation scope and sequential frame-dump policy. Keep every model, argument, check, prerequisite and render mutation phase. Measure the same clean commit with pinned Verilator 5.050. The manager owns full validation, trusted act, hosted evidence and final merge duties. The merge queue remains #372, #423, #504, #517; no second final candidate starts while a predecessor remains unmerged.

[A173] TAKEN
Branch: `517-bounded-simulation-pool`, cut by A10 through `gh issue develop` from dev `483a133ed08867ea0d300d2b4a027b5b48a4282f`
Authoritative references: #517 body and the [A10 assignment](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/517#issuecomment-5779519215); REQUIREMENTS REQ-VER-01/02/04; CONTRIBUTING sections 2 and 3; AGENTS sections 5 to 8; `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`; `scripts/run_all_suites.sh`; `scripts/suite_tally.py`; `tb/verilator/milan_dp/{Makefile,README.md,render_mutants.py,sim_main.cpp,sim_nxn.cpp,sim_prune.cpp,sim_aclk.cpp}`; the linked 478-r1 throughput evidence at `8326a88`.
Interpreted scope: Replace only the ten ordinary executable lines at the tail of the `milan_dp` `run` recipe (`obj_dir`, `obj_notify`, `obj_nxn`, `obj_nxndv`, `obj_nxn8`, `obj_nxn4c`, `obj_nolpf`, `obj_prune`, `obj_ax1x1`, `obj_aclk`; no arguments; run from `tb/verilator/milan_dp`) with one suite-local runner. It runs at most two legs at once by default and one at a time on request. It always runs one at a time, in legacy order, when `MILAN_COUNTER_FRAME_OUT` is present in the environment, even empty. Each leg's stdout and stderr go to its own capture file. The runner replays the captures in legacy order, with the legacy banner and command echo. The bound is an explicit make variable passed as an argument, never derived from `MAKEFLAGS` or `-j`. Values other than 1 and 2 are refused before any leg starts. A nonzero, signalled or unstartable leg fails the recipe, and `render_mutants.py` still runs only after all ten pass. SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP kill and reap every leg's process group. The runner then prints each started leg's partial output with its state and re-raises the signal. Builds, gPTP prerequisites, `render_mutants.py`, models, arguments, seeds, timers, windows and checks are unchanged. There is no timeout, workflow, act, firmware, RTL, pin or ratchet change.
Validation plan: failure-sensitive runner tests with fake legs covering nonzero, crash, missing, out-of-order completion, complete logs, the two-child ceiling, invalid counts, inherited `-j`, interrupt with descendants and no survivors, and sequential frame-dump selection. A write-set audit of the ten real executables runs before concurrency is enabled. Complete local `milan_dp` runs use pinned Verilator 5.050 at the committed head, one worker against two, cold and warm, under the same host limits. They compare per-leg transcripts and tallies, and sample concurrency and peak memory. Then `suite_tally.py --verdict`, `test_render_phase_observation.py`, and the docs, em-dash, contents, Python/shell idiom, hygiene, test-evidence, fail-fast and TODO gates. Hosted timing, trusted act, full banks, reviews and merge stay with A10.
Blockers: none

The Opus author A173 on #517 and external reviewer R244-1 on PR #519 terminated with exit 1 and an explicit usage-limit error. The provider reports reset on September 25 at 16:00 Europe/Warsaw. Neither session produced a final handoff or verdict; no completion or approval is inferred from partial receipts.

#517 remains In progress at committed base `483a133ed08867ea0d300d2b4a027b5b48a4282f`, with two unfinished, untracked runner/test files preserved. A176 Codex now takes the sole author slot in the existing issue branch. The scope, benchmark acceptance and source isolation remain unchanged. For the recovered Codex implementation, R245 is reserved as an independent internal Codex reviewer and R246 as the external Opus reviewer.

R243 continues the independent source review of PR #519. R244's external review remains pending and will restart with fresh context when Opus is available. The frozen source is unchanged. Required cross-system review is retained; #519 cannot merge on the interrupted attempt. Codex implementation and validation continue for ready work while that external capacity is unavailable. This updates the activity snapshot in #415 comment 5780148502.

Blocker found during the required pre-edit write-set audit: `sim_nxn.cpp:402-409` calls endstation_builder with a tracked config and a private -o directory, but `sw/builder/endstation_builder.py:5666-5671` redirects the per-config shape header to `configs/generated/<config>/gen/adp_shape_defaults.svh` and writes it unconditionally. This is an additional shared mutable dependency beyond the frame dump. I will publish the exact affected legs and decision options before implementing dependent concurrency.

[A176] SHARED MUTABLE DEPENDENCY / DECISION REQUIRED

The pre-concurrency audit found an additional write outside the private `sim_nxn` image directory at base `483a133ed08867ea0d300d2b4a027b5b48a4282f`:

- `tb/verilator/milan_dp/sim_nxn.cpp:255-260,402-409,1657`: each sim_nxn executable runs `endstation_builder.py` on its tracked shape config with private `-o`, but without an option suppressing per-config header writes.
- `sw/builder/endstation_builder.py:4255,5666-5671`: the config source is repository-relative; for `configs/...`, `_write_shape_copies` unconditionally writes `configs/generated/<name>/gen/adp_shape_defaults.svh`. Neither `write_rtl` nor `write_fragment` guards this write.
- `obj_nxn`, `obj_nxndv`, and `obj_nxn4c` therefore share `configs/generated/endstation_arty_4x4/gen/adp_shape_defaults.svh`. `obj_notify` writes the 1x1 TDM8 header; `obj_nxn8` writes the 8x8 header. Identical intended bytes do not make simultaneous truncate/write safe. The existing `sim_nxn.cpp:399` comment that private `-o` touches nothing tracked is inaccurate.
- The 109 resolved HDL sources contain readmemh inputs but no simulation file-output operations. The other three selected C++ harness sources have no file-write calls. The optional shared frame dump remains the separate, already-settled whole-set serialization case.

Decision options:
1. Keep source/model/generator argv unchanged and serialize the five sim_nxn legs as one exclusive group, while allowing independent ordinary legs beside that group within the two-child ceiling. Preserve their original relative order. This acknowledges the existing generated-header writes rather than claiming all simulation inputs remain read-only. Measure the resulting full-suite gain.
2. Stop dependent #517 implementation until a separate, publicly scoped generator fix makes those writes private; then retain the original unrestricted two-worker ordinary pool.

Recommendation: option 1 is the smallest runner-local response, but it requires an explicit public scope decision because the current contract assumes read-only generated inputs. I have not enabled ordinary concurrency or changed source files. Independent runner cleanup/failure tests and factual evidence preparation can proceed while this is resolved.

No real ordinary pool has run concurrently under that premise, and no speed result or source approval is claimed.

Serialize all five sim_nxn legs as one exclusive group, preserving their original relative order. Other audited independent ordinary simulations may run alongside that group, within the existing total limit of two children. Preserve every generator/executable argument and existing write/output semantics. Presence of MILAN_COUNTER_FRAME_OUT, including an empty value, still forces the entire ten-command set into original sequential order. No generator or model behavior changes belong to this correction.

Amend the incorrect read-only sentence explicitly before dependent implementation resumes. Require black-box controls that detect overlapping members of the shared group, wrong relative order, lost execution and exceeding the total child limit; a control must show that an independent leg can overlap the group. A planted removal of exclusivity must fail for shared-state contention. Record all affected tracked-header bytes before/after real benchmarks and final source integrity.
